# Pinned supply-chain tooling. Installed into `.venv-audit`, never into `.venv`.
#
# Why a second environment. `pip-audit` and `pip-licenses` bring 29 transitive
# packages with them — three times the whole pinned dev toolchain (`dev.txt`),
# and among them `requests`, `urllib3` and `certifi`, a network client stack
# NFR-4 keeps out of this project's runtime. Installing that set beside `ruff`,
# `mypy` and `pytest` would mean the environment that vouches for the code is
# mostly made of packages nobody chose, and a resolver conflict in one of them
# could change what the gate enforces. Both tools can inspect another
# environment from outside it — `pip-licenses --python`, `pip-audit --path`
# and `-r` — so the separation costs nothing but this file.
#
# STACK.md §2.2 records why these two tools exist at all. Set it up with:
#
#     python3 -m venv .venv-audit
#     .venv-audit/bin/pip install -r .github/requirements/audit.txt
#
# NOT hash-locked, for the same reason `dev.txt` is not, and with the same
# next step. Do not describe this file as hash-locked until it is.
#
# Bumping: Dependabot opens the PR (.github/dependabot.yml watches this
# directory). Regenerate the transitive block with `pip freeze` from a clean
# install of the two direct pins.
#
# A Dependabot PR against a line below is a signal, not a patch to merge. It
# names one package, and what this block has to be is the whole resolution of
# the two direct pins — so merging the single line pins a version the resolver
# does not produce. PR #18 demonstrated that twice: it offered filelock 4.0.0,
# was force-pushed to 4.2.0 while being reviewed, and a clean install resolved
# 4.2.2 both times. Its CI was green on the second of those, which is the whole
# point — a green tick on a single-package bump says the tree still builds, not
# that the pin is the one a clean install produces. Take the PR as notice that
# the block has drifted, do the regeneration above, and close it.
#
# `pip freeze` is the source of the versions, not of the text. This block is
# sorted case-insensitively ignoring `-` and `_`, and spells each name as PyPI
# does; `pip freeze` prints the dist-info spelling (`pip_api`) and sorts its own
# way, so pasting its output wholesale produces a thirty-line diff in which the
# two real changes cannot be seen. Compare by normalised name and edit the
# versions that moved.

# Direct
pip-audit==2.10.1
pip-licenses==5.5.5

# constrained. Generated from a working environment with `pip freeze`.
